lessons.t: Note Values and Time Signatures Review
learn: Review: whole (4 beats), half (2), quarter (1), eighth (1/2) and sixteenth (1/4) notes in 4/4 time.
6/8 time has six eighth-note beats, felt in two groups of three.
Counting aloud ("1 e and a") keeps rhythms accurate.
check: A sixteenth note lasts ___ of a beat in 4/4.
lessons.try: Clap a rhythm in 6/8, feeling two big beats.

learn: Syncopation shifts accents to off-beats or weak beats.
It creates surprise and drive in jazz, funk, Latin and pop music.
Ties across beats are a common way to write syncopation.
lessons.try: Clap a steady beat with your foot and a syncopated pattern with your hands.

learn: A triplet fits three notes in the space of two.
Swing rhythm plays pairs of eighth notes long-short, like a triplet feel.
Swing is central to jazz.
check: A triplet fits ___ notes in the space of two.
lessons.try: Say "trip-a-let" over a steady beat, then swing a simple melody.

units.t: Major and Minor Scales and Key Signatures

learn: A half step is the smallest distance on a piano: from a key to the very next key.
A whole step equals two half steps.
Sharps (♯) raise a note a half step; flats (♭) lower it.
check: A whole step equals ___ half steps.
lessons.try: Find whole and half steps on a keyboard.

learn: A key signature shows sharps or flats used throughout a piece.
G major has one sharp (F♯); F major has one flat (B♭).
The circle of fifths organises keys by number of sharps and flats.
check: F major has one flat on...
lessons.try: Write the key signatures for C, G, D and F major.

learn: Every major key has a relative minor that shares its key signature.
The relative minor starts on the sixth note of the major scale: A minor for C major.
E minor is the relative minor of G major.
check: The relative minor of C major is...
E minor is the relative of...
lessons.try: Play C major and A minor scales and compare their moods.

learn: A triad is a three-note chord built in thirds: root, third, fifth.
C major triad: C, E, G. A minor triad: A, C, E.
Major triads sound bright; minor triads sound darker.
lessons.try: Play C, F and G major triads on a keyboard.

learn: Chords are named with Roman numerals: I, IV, V in a major key.
I-IV-V-I is one of the most common progressions.
Many pop songs use I-V-vi-IV.
check: In C major, the V chord is...
lessons.try: Play I-IV-V-I in C major: C, F, G, C.

learn: Consonant intervals sound stable and restful.
Dissonant intervals sound tense and want to resolve.
Composers use tension and release to create drama.
lessons.try: Play a dissonant pair of notes and resolve it.

learn: Medieval church music included Gregorian chant: a single melodic line sung in Latin without accompaniment.
This texture is called monophony.
Hildegard of Bingen (1098-1179) was a famous medieval composer.
lessons.try: Listen to a Gregorian chant and describe its texture.

learn: Troubadours were travelling poet-musicians who sang about love and adventure.
Medieval instruments included the lute, recorder and hurdy-gurdy.
Dance music like the estampie was popular.
lessons.try: Compare sacred and secular medieval music.

learn: Renaissance music used polyphony: several independent melodic lines at once.
Josquin des Prez and Giovanni Palestrina wrote masses and motets.
Madrigals were secular songs for several voices.
check: A secular song for voices is a...
lessons.try: Sing a round like "Row, Row, Row Your Boat" to experience polyphony.

learn: The Baroque period lasted about 1600-1750.
Johann Sebastian Bach, George Frideric Handel and Antonio Vivaldi were leading composers.
Baroque music features ornamentation, a steady bass line (basso continuo) and the harpsichord.
check: A Baroque keyboard instrument is the...
lessons.try: Listen to "Spring" from Vivaldi's "The Four Seasons".

learn: The Classical period lasted about 1750-1820.
Music became balanced and clear, with homophony (melody plus accompaniment).
Haydn, Mozart and the young Beethoven were leading composers.
lessons.try: Listen to Mozart's "Eine kleine Nachtmusik".

learn: Haydn is called the "Father of the Symphony"; he wrote 104.
A symphony is a large work for orchestra, usually in four movements.
Sonata form has exposition, development and recapitulation.
check: The section where themes return is the...
lessons.try: Listen for the return of the main theme in a symphony movement.

learn: The Romantic period lasted about 1820-1900.
Music became more emotional and dramatic, with bigger orchestras.
Composers included Beethoven (late works), Chopin, Tchaikovsky and Brahms.
lessons.try: Listen to part of Tchaikovsky's "Nutcracker".

learn: Program music tells a story or paints a picture, like Mussorgsky's "Pictures at an Exhibition".
Nationalism used folk songs and dances from composers' homelands.
Dvořák's "New World Symphony" (1893) was inspired by America.
lessons.try: Listen to program music and draw what you imagine.

learn: Impressionist composers like Claude Debussy created dreamy, colourful sounds.
Igor Stravinsky's "The Rite of Spring" (1913) shocked audiences with rhythm and dissonance.
Composers experimented with new scales, rhythms and electronic sounds.
lessons.try: Listen to Debussy's "Clair de lune" and describe its mood.

learn: The voice is produced when air from the lungs vibrates the vocal folds in the larynx.
The mouth, throat and nose shape the sound.
Good posture and breath support help you sing well.
check: The voice is made when air vibrates the...
lessons.try: Practise breathing from the diaphragm.

learn: Voice types from high to low: soprano, alto, tenor, bass.
During adolescence, voices change, especially for boys.
Changing voices are normal; sing gently in a comfortable range.
lessons.try: Find the comfortable range of your voice.

learn: Choirs combine voices in harmony.
Blend means voices sound unified; balance means no part is too loud.
Warm up the voice before singing.
lessons.try: Sing a two-part round with classmates.

learn: Microphones turn sound waves into electrical signals.
Digital audio stores sound as numbers sampled thousands of times per second.
A digital audio workstation (DAW) records and edits music on a computer.
lessons.try: Record a short sound on a device and play it back.

learn: Synthesisers create sound electronically.
MIDI sends instructions (which note, how loud) between instruments and computers.
Loops are repeated sections used to build songs.
check: Repeated sections used to build songs are...
lessons.try: Build a beat from loops using the music keyboard.

learn: Mixing balances the volume and position of each track.
Effects like reverb add space.
Respect copyright: use your own music or music you have permission to use.
lessons.try: Mix a short two-track piece.

units.t: Music of Latin America and the Caribbean

learn: Cuban son and salsa use the clave rhythm as their foundation.
Reggae from Jamaica emphasises off-beats.
Calypso from Trinidad features witty lyrics and steelpan.
lessons.try: Clap the 3-2 son clave rhythm.

learn: Brazilian samba and bossa nova blend African and Portuguese influences.
Argentine tango uses the bandoneón, a type of accordion.
Andean music uses panpipes (zampoña) and the charango.
lessons.try: Listen to Andean panpipe music.

learn: Mariachi features violins, trumpets, vihuela and guitarrón.
Son jarocho from Veracruz uses the jarana guitar and dancing on a wooden platform.
Corridos are story songs about history and heroes.
lessons.try: Listen to a mariachi piece and name its instruments.

learn: Lyrics tell a story or express a feeling.
Use rhyme, repetition and imagery.
The chorus carries the main message and repeats.
check: The main message is often in the...
lessons.try: Write a verse and chorus about something you care about.

learn: Choose a key and chord progression, like I-V-vi-IV.
Write a melody that fits the chords and the natural rhythm of the words.
Make the chorus melody memorable.
lessons.try: Set your lyrics to a melody over four chords.

learn: Arrange your song with an introduction, verses, choruses and an ending.
Choose instruments and dynamics to build energy.
Perform or record your song and reflect on it.
lessons.try: Perform or record your song for the class.
